body:
I think that the issue isnt that username doesnt get populated, but rather that there exists codepaths which use username, and not email. 

Instead of chopping and gluing we should rather fix that, so that the user is defined by the field that is set, email, username, Provider identity and so on.

Have you tried 0.26?

It would be helpful to hear how that works with your setup, and particularly, if you could set up a separate test setup from scratch with a new database and your oidc setup and how that behaves.

I'm going to close this PR, the other issue seem to have become a bit of a mix of different issues, it would be great if you test like mentioned above and then create a new issue with your observation on 0.26 for both your current setup and for a clean setup.

Yes, I've meant from 0.24 this is happening and in the issue I've references I said it has worsen with 0.26: https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/issues/2475#issuecomment-2881583450

We use Google OAuth 2.0, which does not provide the custom preferred_username claim.
What happens in 0.26 is a new user comes from the OIDC, his username is left blank, and is created in the sqlite table for the users. Then when next one comes, his username is also blank and the creation fails with: 
```
ERR http internal server error error="creating or updating user: constraint failed: UNIQUE constraint failed: users.name (2067)" code=500
```

Because the first user already exists with the blank username.

I haven't tested from scratch as it is difficult for me to reset or setup a separate test instance. The issue occurs with existing db which was gradually updated from version 0.22.1 onward. Now on 0.26.0. These are the indexes from the sqlite db in our instance: It appears this migration hasn't been run: https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/blob/d2879b2b3675c6c38b1a39dd7a7b44c1679287a9/hscontrol/db/db.go#L544 Despite having it in the migrations table: I suppose I have to manually update the table to have the expected indexes?

> The issue occurs with existing db which was gradually updated from version 0.22.1 onward. Now on 0.26.0.

While it should not, doing gradually upgrades _might_ be a problem if you did every .patch release and so on. It is very strange tho that it didnt pick up the migration...

If you take a backup, you could try to delete it from the migration table to force it to run again. 

If it is an option, and you can sanitise the database and send it to me, that might be helpful. If this is an option, getting the old 0.22.1 version and the 0.26.0 version would be helpful.

I've fixed my DB indexes and successfully logged with two test users from our Google OAuth 2.0 OIDC provider. Here are the new users without usernames as listed by the CLI `headscale users list`: Thank you for the help resolving the issue. As for the DB, I can send you the DDL only, cannot risk sanitizing the data and missing something. Is that something of your interest?

ah great, can you post your findings from this on the issue so others can check if they are also missing the update?

DDL wont be that helpful, but its ok, glad you fixed it.
actually, you can email me the ddl, find my email in my github
